answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed when peers prove misbehavior, so creating thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Like tending an orchard, reputation grows slowly through verified completed work and decays if an agent vanishes or cheats, so a dune of throwaway accounts cannot outvote established participants. At the zenith of trust, high-stakes roles require both long history and locked collateral, making an attack cost more than any gain from flooding the network with sock puppets.
